title: Linear Search
directAnswer: Loop by index; return `i` the first time `nums[i] == target`. If the loop finishes, return -1.

remember.takeaway: Linear search is the fallback when data has no structure.
remember.formula: for i,x in nums: if x==target return i; return -1

problemStatement: Given an integer array `nums` and a `target`, return the index of the first occurrence of `target`, or `-1` if it is absent.
understanding: Scan left to right and return the index as soon as you hit the target.

approaches.name: Sequential scan
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
With no assumptions about order, the only way to find a value is to look at elements one at a time and return the index of the first match. Falling off the end means it's absent, so return -1.

**Why return on first match.** The problem asks for the *first* occurrence, so returning immediately gives the smallest index. Continuing would either waste work or (if you overwrite) return the last index instead.

**Why -1 for 'not found'.** A sentinel out of the valid index range (0..n−1) cleanly signals absence; the caller checks `result == -1`. Returning 0 or throwing would be ambiguous or heavy.

**When you can do better.** Linear search is the fallback for *unstructured* data. If the array were sorted, binary search drops this to O(log n); if you query repeatedly, a hash set/map gives O(1) lookups after O(n) setup. Naming those alternatives shows you reach for structure when it exists.
hints: No ordering is given — what's the only guaranteed way to find the value?
Return the index on the first match to get the first occurrence.
If the loop ends with no match, return -1.
approaches.insight: If the array were sorted you'd use binary search (O(log n)) — calling that out shows range awareness.
approaches.complexityReasoning: in the worst case (absent or last) you scan all n elements; best case is the first element.

dryRun.intro: Scan left to right, return on first match.

pitfalls: Returning the element value instead of its index.

commonMistakes: Returning the element instead of its index.

followupVariations.title: Binary Search
followupVariations.hint: O(log n) when the array is sorted.

followupVariations.title: Count Occurrences
followupVariations.hint: Don't stop early — tally all matches.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Sequential scan. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.

interviewerIntent.testing: Whether you handle the not-found case and know when structure beats a linear scan.
interviewerIntent.commonMistake: Returning the value, or omitting the -1 case.
interviewerIntent.toStandOut: Mention binary search (sorted) and hash lookup (repeated queries) as faster alternatives.

clarifyingQuestions.question: First or any occurrence?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: I return the first; I'd adjust if any index is acceptable.

clarifyingQuestions.question: Is the array sorted?
clarifyingQuestions.answer: If it is, I'd switch to binary search for O(log n).
